title: Add low-overhead NVTX & per-kernel traces for kernel selection and prefill/decode scheduling
creator: Sofia Lin
description:
Problem:
Current runtime lacks consistent, structured telemetry for per-kernel latency and the decisions the kernel selector makes during prefill and decode. We have ad-hoc NVTX ranges and occasional CUDA event logging in experiments, but there is no stable mapping from: incoming request attributes (model, seq_len, batch_size, quant_type, attention path) -> kernel variant chosen -> per-kernel exec time. This makes it hard to debug regressions introduced by kernel scheduling changes, attention optimizations (e.g., flash attention fallbacks), or prefill/decode scheduling heuristics.

Goal:
Create a low-overhead, production-safe tracing envelope that: 1) emits NVTX ranges and structured trace spans at key decision points (kernel selector evaluation, attention kernel entry/exit, prefill start/end, decode step scheduling), 2) attaches per-kernel metadata (kernel name/id, algorithm variant, sequence length, batch size, quantization, device id), and 3) records per-kernel metrics (wall time, CUDA event time, occupancies when available). Expose these spans to the existing tracing pipeline (Jaeger/Zipkin/Datadog) and improve Grafana dashboards to surface regressions and hot kernels.

Non-goal:
We are NOT rearchitecting full continuous performance sampling for every token in prod. The initial effort is focused on enabling deterministic, low-overhead traces in production plus an opt-in high-detail mode for staging and perf runs.
acceptance_criteria: Instrument kernel selector path to emit a structured trace span with chosen kernel metadata for every kernel decision in prefill and decode (prefill and decode phases distinguishable)
Annotate attention kernel entry/exit with NVTX ranges that include sequence length, batch size, and attention algorithm tag (e.g., flash, unfused, fallback)
Implement a lightweight per-kernel timer that uses a single CUDA event pair but avoids per-token events in steady-state production (sampling rate configurable)
Tracing payloads are forwarded to our tracing backend and include standard tags: model, model_version, route_id, request_id, customer_tier, device_id, kernel_id, seq_len, batch_size, quant_type
Add Grafana dashboard panels showing per-kernel p50/p95 latency, kernel selection distribution for common seq_len buckets, and correlation charts for latency vs kernel choice
Add unit/integration tests for the instrumentation (simulated kernels) and a perf-run check that fails if overhead > 2% at 99th percentile for a representative decode workload
Document instrumentation guidelines in the runtime CONTRIBUTING.md and add a short runbook for interpreting traces
Code PR merged, rollout to staging with opt-in high-detail traces, then gradual rollout to production with sampling enabled

notes: Trade-offs discussed: full per-token instrumentation yields better fidelity but unacceptable overhead in prod. We chose sampling + low-overhead spans for production and full-trace mode for perf/staging.
Implementation approach: lightweight tracing API that defers heavy string allocations; uses integer IDs for kernels and a lookup table emitted by build-time metadata to keep span payload small.
Potential future work: export per-kernel GPU occupancy and SM utilization if supported by drivers; correlate with hardware counters for deeper perf analysis.
Risk: incorrect kernel_id mapping can mislead investigations. Add deterministic bake-time registry and test that kernel_id -> name mapping is stable across builds.
